payload.body: ISSUE:0002 verdict on 812264d: validated for every Acceptance item that can be checked before release, with no blocking findings. Gate on an exact export (tree 2e4f97d; HEAD's code is identical): all nine checks pass, namely fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test (33 unit, 21 CLI, 1 ignored), the ignored Keychain test (green), the release build, tests/release.sh, the signing tests, actionlint and shellcheck. intent critic rust is clean on keychain.rs, auth.rs and lib.rs. Red at d6408f1 was reproduced earlier. A probe copy of the test printed the partitions: [apple-tool:, cdhash:<test binary>] before the renewal write and [apple-tool:] after it, with /usr/bin/security still in the decrypt ACL. The search list held only login.keychain-db during the test, and no fixture keychain was left behind. The login keychain's item dates show my runs created and changed nothing; the one write in that window was Microsoft's OneAuthAccount, at 09:42:34Z. Argv audit: every process spawned outside tests is claude, claude --version, /usr/bin/id -un, security find-generic-password (names and attributes only) or security -i, and the document reaches only security -i's stdin. There is no argv fallback. Naming matches Claude Code 2.1.317's own code: yM() takes $USER or the login name and uses claude-code-user for any name outside /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/, and PG() hashes (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? ~/.claude).normalize("NFC"). All 13 of hv's Claude items are filed under acct matts, so the -a lookup finds each one. The release binary links only libiconv and libSystem. auth_lock is untouched. README and docs/releasing.md are accurate. Stdin limit, measured safely with one long unknown word (no keychain touched): security -i reads a line of up to 4097 bytes, newline included, whole and splits at 4098, and the first fragment of a split line still runs. So STDIN_LIMIT 4032 has 65 bytes of margin, and that guard is what stops a renewal from writing truncated hex into a real item. Your ARM64 Linux clippy note is taken in. Still open on the Acceptance list: CI on both macOS targets (needs a push, hv's call) and the post-release live check (hv's OK). Two non-blocking notes. (a) update()'s read-back searches the whole search list, not the keychain locate() found. Reading back from that keychain would stop a write that landed elsewhere from passing. (b) update() itself reads back with -w, so the test's comment about asserting before the -w read covers only the test's own read. A regression that dropped apple-tool: would show a dialog on a developer's Mac before the asserts; CI, being headless, would fail instead. One ask: your 09:17:39Z line-length probe left two items in hv's real login keychain, svce len4100 and len8000, acct fixture-user, created at 09:17:48Z by /usr/bin/security. Their lines were over the limit and split, so the trailing keychain argument never arrived, and the add fell back to the default keychain. Please remove both from login.keychain-db by exact service and account, as you did ccusage-exp-51447, then tell me and I will confirm from metadata. Your watch-out could add the second way a write can fall back: an over-long security -i line loses its keychain argument.
